verification_log.detail: The effective requirement set under `--change <id>` is defined at spec.md:360-367: 'resolve requirement identifiers against the archived capability specs, with the active change's spec delta taking precedence ... Requirements belonging to other in-flight changes SHALL be neither citable nor excludable', reinforced at spec.md:509-511. The set is a function of (openspec/specs/, openspec/changes/<id>/specs/) and of nothing else on the branch. Scenario other-changes-are-invisible (spec.md:404-410) makes naming another in-flight change's requirement a FAILURE, so the other 30-odd directories in the tree are not merely ignored, they are actively unreachable. The 11 uncited gen-eval-framework requirements from extract-gen-eval-package / factory-missions-architecture-alignment / rename-descriptor-model-levels therefore cannot enter a `--change <batched-id>` run's effective set. R6-F1 is genuinely dissolved, not relocated. Downstream check: those three changes will each have to cite their own new requirements when THEY reach the queue, which is satisfiable by their own authors (their own delta IS in their own effective set) and is exactly what D13 reverse enforcement exists to force.

findings.title: `openspec/changes/archive/` is excluded from union mode but not from change-id derivation - every archive PR derives `--change archive`, or fails as ambiguous
findings.description:
R6-N1 taught union mode to exclude `openspec/changes/archive/`, and spec.md:513-517 states the reason at length ('Archived deltas SHALL NOT be unioned: they have already been merged into openspec/specs/ ...'). That exclusion was never propagated to the OTHER thing this plan does with `openspec/changes/` - the change-id DERIVATION - even though 737c1161 rewrote the derivation rule to cover a second event.

The derivation is specified as 'a change id from the change directory under `openspec/changes/` touched by the diff' (spec.md:533-535) and, new in this commit, 'the set of change directories touched by the diff against the merge group's base commit' (spec.md:540-542). `archive` is a directory directly under `openspec/changes/`. Nothing in spec.md, tasks.md:656-678, design.md:485-496 or work-packages.yaml:434-441 excludes it.

DEMONSTRATED, NOT INFERRED. Every change in this repository completes with a `chore(openspec): archive <id>` commit that git-moves `openspec/changes/<id>/` into `openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<id>/`. Running the plan's derivation verbatim against three real archive commits on main:

    $ for c in 247bc201 600744a5 9a167621; do \
        git diff --name-only ${c}^ ${c} -- openspec/changes/ \
        | sed 's#^openspec/changes/\([^/]*\)/.*#\1#' | sort -u; done
    archive
    archive
    archive

So on `pull_request` the job derives exactly one 'change id' - the literal string `archive` - and invokes the BLOCKING gate with `--change archive`. The count is one, so the SKIP does not fire and the ambiguity rule does not fire. `openspec/changes/archive/` exists but has no `specs/` subdirectory, so `--change archive` resolves to a zero-requirement delta: the blocking merge-candidate run silently degrades to archive-only resolution. Nothing in the plan defines that behaviour, and task 3.16's 'unresolvable inputs are errors, never empty scopes' (tasks.md:439) does not catch it, because the path is not unresolvable - it exists.

The outcome is worse if the implementer suppresses rename detection, which is the natural defensive choice for a derivation that must be deterministic:

    $ git show --name-only --no-renames --pretty=format: 247bc201 \
        | grep '^openspec/changes/' \
        | sed 's#^openspec/changes/\([^/]*\)/.*#\1#' | sort -u
    archive
    derive-descriptors-from-contracts

Two touched change directories. On `pull_request` that is the ambiguity rule (spec.md:537-538: 'Where it touches more than one, it SHALL fail as ambiguous rather than choosing'), so the blocking sweep HARD-REDS every archive pull request in the repository. On `merge_group` it invokes the gate twice, once with a real id whose directory no longer exists on the branch and once with `archive`.

So the rule's outcome on the single most routine OpenSpec PR class in this repo is either (a) undefined-but-silently-degraded or (b) hard failure, selected by an unstated `git diff` flag. Both are defects the plan currently invites, and an implementer writing test_ci_sweep_wiring.py has no case telling them which is intended.

This is the same failure mode the last five rounds found: the fix landed in the artifact the finding named (union mode, spec.md:513-517) while the artifact owning the consequence - the derivation rule, one requirement paragraph below it - went stale.

WHAT SHOULD CHANGE. State the exclusion once, normatively, in the spec delta where the derivation is defined: derivation SHALL consider only change directories directly under `openspec/changes/` other than `archive/`, on both blocking events; a diff touching only `openspec/changes/archive/` is the SKIP, not a derived id and not an ambiguity. Mirror it in tasks.md's per-event table (656-678) and in wp-wiring's dispatch summary (work-packages.yaml:434-441), add an archive-PR scenario so the derivation is pinned by a test, and name the diff invocation precisely enough that rename detection cannot change the answer.

findings.title: D12 contradicts itself: 'Two touched directories is a genuine ambiguity and fails rather than guessing' is now false for one of the two blocking events
findings.description:
737c1161 rewrote D12's 'Why `merge_group` iterates instead of unioning' paragraph (design.md:433-454) and correctly closes it with 'The ambiguity rule therefore applies on `pull_request` only' (design.md:453-454). It did not touch the paragraph 31 lines later, inside the same decision:

    design.md:485  **The blocking job derives its change id from the diff, and skips when there is
    design.md:486  none.** ... CI
    design.md:488  triggers on unfiltered `pull_request` and `merge_group`, so `dependabot/*`,
    design.md:489  `chore/*`, and `codex/*` all reach the job. ...
    design.md:494  ... Two touched directories is a
    design.md:495  genuine ambiguity and fails rather than guessing.

When that paragraph was written only `pull_request` derived, so 'the blocking job' was singular and the sentence was true. After this commit both blocking events derive from the diff, the paragraph explicitly names `merge_group` as reaching the job, and its closing sentence states the exact rule spec.md:543 and tasks.md:663-665 say must NOT fire there.

Not rated blocking: the correct rule is stated three times in artifacts the implementer is actually routed through (spec.md:543, tasks.md:663-665, work-packages.yaml:437), wp-wiring says 'Task 5.7 carries the full per-event table - follow it exactly', and the contradicting sentence sits 31 lines after a same-decision paragraph that already qualifies it. Fix by qualifying design.md:494-495 with 'on `pull_request`' and cross-referencing the merge_group rule.

findings.title: wp-wiring's test-file mapping traded a precise five-scenario list for a pointer to a nine-scenario list, two of which are gate-verdict scenarios the wiring test cannot own
findings.description:
To stay under the 4000-char description limit (the commit message records hitting it twice; the description is now 3907 chars), 737c1161 replaced

    covering all five wiring scenarios (SKIP, unresolvable-base FAILURE, merge_group
    union-and-block, push-to-main exiting zero despite findings, and no `if:` guard)

with

    covering every scenario named on task 5.7's `Spec scenarios` line.

That line (tasks.md:604) now names nine scenarios, and two of them - '(an opted-in surface fails the sweep)' and '(a surface that has not opted in is reported, not failed)' - are gate-verdict scenarios owned by the enforcement work (phase 3 and task 4.3), not CI-wiring scenarios. test_ci_sweep_wiring.py drives the job's extracted bash fragment; it can assert argv and exit-status propagation, not whether an opted-in surface produces a violation. An implementer taking the instruction literally will either duplicate gate tests inside a bash harness or write a shallow assertion that proves nothing.

Not blocking - the seven genuinely-wiring scenarios on that line are the ones a bash-fragment harness naturally reaches, and no wrong production code follows. Fix by re-listing the wiring scenarios explicitly (there are now seven: SKIP, ambiguity, unresolvable-base ERROR, merge-group-iterates, merge-group-ignores-unbatched, push-to-main cannot fail, no event guard) and dropping the two verdict scenarios from the mapping.

findings.title: `merge-group-ignores-unbatched-changes` asserts a property of the gate's effective requirement set but is listed only under the wiring task
findings.description:
The new scenario's THEN clause is 'those changes' requirements SHALL NOT enter any blocking invocation's effective requirement set'. The effective requirement set is a gate-resolution concept (spec.md:360-367, task 3.16, test_resolution_modes.py). The scenario is referenced only from task 5.7's `Spec scenarios` line (tasks.md:604), whose test file is test_ci_sweep_wiring.py, which observes argv and exit codes - not requirement sets.

The scenario is still testable as written up in verification_log C4: a wiring test can assert the gate is invoked exactly once, with the batched id, and never bare, which combined with 3.16's resolution tests establishes the property. Recorded because the coverage is transitive rather than direct, so a reader asking 'which test proves this scenario' will not find one that literally asserts its THEN. Either add the scenario to task 3.16's `Spec scenarios` line as its resolution-side owner, or restate the THEN in argv terms ('the gate SHALL NOT be invoked without `--change`, and SHALL NOT be invoked with an id the diff does not touch').

findings.title: 5.7c's new 'record but do not gate' half names no destination, so nothing can later confirm it ran
findings.description:
The brief asks whether 'record but do not gate' is checkable. Strictly: no. Nothing consumes the union run's output, so 'did not gate' is the default and is unfalsifiable, and the note names no file to write the recording to - so a later reader cannot distinguish 'ran it and recorded a non-zero exit' from 'skipped it'.

Not rated blocking, and not a regression: 5.7c is `[human]`, owned by no package, and its GATING half has the same property - 'record the exit code' (tasks.md:723-724) also names no destination, and that has stood through six rounds. The new half is no weaker than the task containing it, and its instruction to a human is unambiguous ('It must not be made to pass - it unions every in-flight change on the branch and will report other changes' uncited requirements').

Cheap improvement if PLAN_FIX is opened anyway for R7-F1: name one destination for both halves, e.g. `openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/reviews/5.7c-capability-sweep.txt`, holding both invocations' commands, exit codes and output. That converts 5.7c from attestation into an artifact and makes the gating/union distinction auditable by whoever reviews the PR rather than only by the person who ran it.

findings.title: Confirmed clean under this round's briefs
findings.description:
Recorded so round 8 does not re-litigate them.

C1 PASSES - the merge_group fix dissolves R6-F1 rather than moving it. `--change <id>` resolution is a function of openspec/specs/ and openspec/changes/<id>/specs/ only (spec.md:360-367, 509-511), and other in-flight changes are actively unreachable rather than merely unread: other-changes-are-invisible (spec.md:404-410) makes naming one a FAILURE. The 34 tree entries under openspec/changes/ on origin/main (re-verified this round; all 34 are directories) therefore cannot leak into a blocking run's effective requirement set. Every blocking invocation is now scoped to a change whose own authors can satisfy it.

C2 PASSES - the invariant holds across all seven described invocations; the enumeration is in verification_log. It is stated in all four load-bearing artifacts, and the anti-inference guard ('The gate SHALL NOT infer blocking from the flag, and SHALL NOT fail merely because `--change` was omitted', spec.md:520-522) correctly prevents the earlier draft's over-correction from returning.

C4 PASSES for both new scenarios - each is red-before / green-after testable in the harness task 5.7 already mandates.

Mechanical checks: `openspec validate trace-requirements-to-contracts --strict` -> 'Change is valid'. 58 gen-eval-framework scenarios, matching the commit message's 57->58 claim. 7 skill-workflow scenarios. work-packages.yaml parses; wp-wiring's description is 3907 chars, under the 4000 limit. Per issue #324 these were treated as no evidence on their own - R7-F1 survives all of them.

Dispatch hygiene: all seven `[human]` tasks (4.1, 4.2, 4.2b, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.7c) are named in the work-packages carve-out and none is inside a package's claimed range without an explicit EXCEPT; 4.3 is unpackaged with a stated reason. wp-wiring's write_allow covers every file tasks 5.6-5.9 must touch, and its DISPATCH PRECONDITION plus the honest accounting of why depends_on cannot express it are unchanged and still correct.

Deliberately NOT flagged: design.md:440 quotes the refuted round-5 draft as history, which the brief identifies as intentional. Confirmed it reads as quotation ('An earlier draft used union mode on `merge_group` instead, reasoning that a merge-group branch "holds precisely the changes that are landing..."') and is refuted in the immediately following sentence.
